en.greeting: Hi! Today you'll learn to give a presentation in English: guide your audience through the talk, explain a chart clearly and handle questions calmly. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: Open your talk
steps.text: A good presentation starts with a clear map. Let's learn how to open.
steps.body: **Signposts** (papan penunjuk jalan) are phrases that tell listeners where they are in your talk. Open in three moves: **greet and thank** (*Good morning, everyone, and thank you for coming.*), **give the topic** (*Today I'd like to talk about …*) and **give the map** (*I've divided my talk into three parts. First, … Then, … Finally, …*). Skip the long apology (*Mohon maaf kalau ada kesalahan* → `Sorry for my bad English` ✗): it's humble in Indonesian, but in English it makes people expect a weak talk. Thank them instead.

pairs.en: Today I'd like to talk about …
I've divided my talk into … parts.
pairs.id: Saya membagi presentasi saya menjadi … bagian.

pairs.en: Please feel free to ask questions at the end.

steps.title: Give the map
steps.text: Build the sentence that tells the audience how your talk is organised.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Saya membagi presentasi saya menjadi tiga bagian.
question.solution: I have divided my talk into three parts.
question.explanation: **I have divided** (I've divided): you made the plan before the talk, and it's ready now, so present perfect. **divide … into** = membagi … menjadi. Then name the parts: *First, … Then, … Finally, …*

steps.title: Move on and finish
steps.text: Now the signs between the parts, and at the end.
steps.body: When one part ends, close it and open the next: **Let's move on to …** / **Now let's look at …** / **That brings me to …** Not `Okay, next. This is the graph.` ✗: *Okay, next* gives no direction, and everyone can see it's a graph. At the end: **To sum up, …** (recap from the meetings lesson), **The key takeaway is that …** (*takeaway* = the main message people take home) and **Thank you for listening. I'm happy to take any questions.** No closing apology needed.

pairs.en: I'm happy to take any questions.
pairs.id: Dengan senang hati saya menjawab pertanyaan.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Help Sari move to her next part.

question.prompt: Sari has finished the first part of her talk, about why customers cancel orders. Her next slide shows the results of a customer survey. Which is the best way to move on?
options: Okay, next. This is the survey.
Let's move on to the results of our customer survey.
Sorry, now I want to change to the survey.
question.explanation: **Let's move on to …** closes one part and tells listeners exactly what comes next. *Okay, next. This is the survey.* gives no direction and states the obvious, and *I want to change to* is *saya mau ganti ke* word for word.

steps.title: Talk about your visuals
steps.text: Charts are where many presentations lose their audience. Here's how to guide people through one.
steps.body: Three moves: **say what it shows** (*This chart shows …*), **point to the part** (*As you can see, …* / *If you look at the left-hand column, …*) and **give the message** (*What's interesting here is that …*). For the message, use your trend words: *rose sharply, peaked at, remained stable, doubled*; **to** + the new level, never `rose until 4,000` ✗. Don't read the slide word for word: the audience reads faster than you speak. Look at them, slow down for numbers, and say it in your own words.

pairs.en: If you look at the left-hand column, …
pairs.id: Kalau Anda melihat kolom sebelah kiri, …

pairs.en: On the right, you can see …
pairs.id: Di sebelah kanan, Anda bisa melihat …

steps.title: Explaining a chart
steps.text: Read these aloud, slowly, with a short pause before each number.
steps.body: The slide, as a table (practice figures): monthly users of a food app in Bandung · January 20,000 · April 35,000 · July 50,000 · October 48,000. Notice the three moves: what it shows, where to look, and the message.

examples.en: This graph shows the number of monthly users of our app in Bandung.
examples.id: Grafik ini menunjukkan jumlah pengguna bulanan aplikasi kita di Bandung.

examples.en: As you can see, the number of users rose steadily from January to July.
examples.id: Seperti yang bisa Anda lihat, jumlah pengguna naik terus dari Januari sampai Juli.

examples.en: In July, it peaked at fifty thousand, and then it fell slightly.
examples.id: Di bulan Juli, jumlahnya mencapai puncak di lima puluh ribu, lalu turun sedikit.

examples.en: What's interesting here is that the number more than doubled in just six months.
examples.id: Yang menarik di sini adalah jumlahnya naik lebih dari dua kali lipat hanya dalam enam bulan.

steps.title: Present the slide
steps.text: Now you present a slide.

question.prompt: Your slide (practice figures): orders per month · Surabaya: January 2,000, June 4,000 · Bandung: January 3,000, June 3,000. Which is the best way to talk about it?
options: Okay, next. This is the chart. Surabaya, two thousand, four thousand. Bandung, three thousand, three thousand.
As you can see, orders in Surabaya rose until 4,000, while orders in Bandung fell sharply.
As you can see, orders in Surabaya doubled, from 2,000 to 4,000, while orders in Bandung remained stable.
question.explanation: It points to the slide (*As you can see*), gives the message (*doubled*, *remained stable*) and matches the figures. The first one just reads the numbers aloud. The second one uses *until* for a level (say *rose to 4,000*), and Bandung didn't fall: it stayed at 3,000.

steps.title: Handle questions
steps.text: Last part: the questions at the end. Here's a simple plan.
steps.body: Four moves: **welcome** (*That's a great question.*), **check** if you're not sure (*If I understand correctly, you're asking …?*), **answer briefly**, then **check back** (*Does that answer your question?*). Don't know? **Don't bluff** (pura-pura tahu): *I'm afraid I don't have that figure with me, but I'll follow up by email.* **I'm afraid** = sayangnya, a polite way to give bad news, not *takut*. An honest follow-up sounds professional; a wrong guess hurts your credibility.

pairs.en: If I understand correctly, you're asking …
pairs.id: Kalau saya tidak salah tangkap, Anda bertanya …

pairs.en: I'm afraid I don't have that figure with me.
pairs.id: Sayangnya saya tidak membawa angka itu.
Akan saya tindak lanjuti lewat email.

pairs.en: I'll check and get back to you.
pairs.id: Akan saya cek lalu saya kabari.

pairs.en: I'll come to that in a minute.

steps.title: Listen and reply
steps.text: Press play and listen to a question from the audience.

question.prompt: You're presenting this year's sales at your company in Jakarta. You don't have the figures for each city with you. Listen to the question. What's the best reply?
question.listen: Thank you for the presentation. Could you tell us the exact sales figure for Medan in December?
options: Sales in Medan were about two billion rupiah, I think. Maybe a bit more.
That's a good question. I'm afraid I don't have the Medan figure with me, but I'll check it and send it to you by email today.
Sorry, I'm afraid of this question. Next question, please.
question.explanation: You don't have the figure, so be honest: welcome the question, say **I'm afraid** (sayangnya) you don't have it, and promise a follow-up. The first reply is a guess, and if it's wrong, people stop trusting your numbers. In the third, *I'm afraid of this question* means 'I'm scared of it', and it doesn't answer at all.

steps.title: Check the question
steps.text: One more: a question you don't fully understand.

question.prompt: At a seminar in Yogyakarta, a student asks a long question about prices, delivery and next year. You aren't sure what she really wants to know. What's the best first reply?
options: Yes. Next question, please.
If I understand correctly, you're asking whether delivery will cost more next year?
Sorry, I don't understand your English.
question.explanation: Check before you answer: **If I understand correctly, you're asking …?** shows you listened and lets her correct you. *Next question* ignores her, and *I don't understand your English* blames her; if you need to, say *Sorry, I'm not sure I follow* (from the meetings lesson).

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's everything on one page. Keep it open while you prepare your next presentation.

examples.id: Mari lanjut ke hasilnya. Seperti yang bisa Anda lihat di grafik ini, penjualan naik tajam di bulan Maret.

examples.en: What's interesting here is that most orders came from Surabaya.

steps.title: Learn more
steps.text: Want more? Here are two short engVid videos with presentation phrases and tips for difficult questions.

id.greeting: Halo! Hari ini kamu belajar presentasi dalam bahasa Inggris: memandu audiens sepanjang presentasi, menjelaskan grafik dengan jelas dan menjawab pertanyaan dengan tenang. Ayo kita mulai langkah demi langkah.

steps.title: Membuka presentasi
steps.text: Presentasi yang baik dimulai dengan peta yang jelas. Ayo belajar cara membukanya.
steps.body: **Signpost** (papan penunjuk jalan) adalah ungkapan yang memberi tahu pendengar mereka sedang di bagian mana. Buka dalam tiga langkah: **beri salam dan terima kasih** (*Good morning, everyone, and thank you for coming.*), **sebutkan topiknya** (*Today I'd like to talk about …*) dan **beri petanya** (*I've divided my talk into three parts. First, … Then, … Finally, …*). Lewati permintaan maaf yang panjang (*Mohon maaf kalau ada kesalahan* → `Sorry for my bad English` ✗): itu rendah hati dalam bahasa Indonesia, tapi dalam bahasa Inggris membuat audiens menduga presentasimu lemah. Ucapkan terima kasih saja.

pairs.en: Today I'd like to talk about …
I've divided my talk into … parts.
pairs.id: Saya membagi presentasi saya menjadi … bagian.

pairs.en: Please feel free to ask questions at the end.

steps.title: Beri petanya
steps.text: Susun kalimat yang memberi tahu audiens bagaimana presentasimu disusun.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Saya membagi presentasi saya menjadi tiga bagian.
question.solution: I have divided my talk into three parts.
question.explanation: **I have divided** (I've divided): kamu membuat rencananya sebelum presentasi, dan sekarang sudah siap, jadi present perfect. **divide … into** = membagi … menjadi. Lalu sebutkan bagian-bagiannya: *First, … Then, … Finally, …*

steps.title: Pindah bagian dan menutup
steps.text: Sekarang tanda-tanda di antara bagian, dan di akhir.
steps.body: Saat satu bagian selesai, tutup lalu buka bagian berikutnya: **Let's move on to …** / **Now let's look at …** / **That brings me to …** Bukan `Okay, next. This is the graph.` ✗: *Okay, next* tidak memberi arah, dan semua orang bisa melihat itu grafik. Di akhir: **To sum up, …** (ulasan dari pelajaran rapat), **The key takeaway is that …** (*takeaway* = pesan utama yang dibawa pulang) dan **Thank you for listening. I'm happy to take any questions.** Tidak perlu minta maaf di penutup.

pairs.en: I'm happy to take any questions.
pairs.id: Dengan senang hati saya menjawab pertanyaan.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Bantu Sari pindah ke bagian berikutnya.

question.prompt: Sari sudah selesai dengan bagian pertama presentasinya, tentang alasan pelanggan membatalkan pesanan. Slide berikutnya menunjukkan hasil survei pelanggan. Cara mana yang paling baik untuk pindah bagian?
options: Okay, next. This is the survey.
Let's move on to the results of our customer survey.
Sorry, now I want to change to the survey.
question.explanation: **Let's move on to …** menutup satu bagian dan memberi tahu pendengar dengan tepat apa yang berikutnya. *Okay, next. This is the survey.* tidak memberi arah dan hanya menyebut yang sudah jelas, dan *I want to change to* adalah *saya mau ganti ke* kata per kata.

steps.title: Membahas visualmu
steps.text: Di bagian grafik, banyak presentasi kehilangan audiensnya. Begini cara memandu mereka.
steps.body: Tiga langkah: **sebutkan apa yang ditunjukkan** (*This chart shows …*), **tunjuk bagiannya** (*As you can see, …* / *If you look at the left-hand column, …*) dan **sampaikan pesannya** (*What's interesting here is that …*). Untuk pesannya, pakai kata-kata tren: *rose sharply, peaked at, remained stable, doubled*; **to** + level barunya, bukan `rose until 4,000` ✗. Jangan membaca slide kata per kata: audiens membaca lebih cepat daripada kamu bicara. Lihat ke mereka, pelan-pelan saat menyebut angka, dan sampaikan dengan kata-katamu sendiri.

pairs.en: If you look at the left-hand column, …
pairs.id: Kalau Anda melihat kolom sebelah kiri, …

pairs.en: On the right, you can see …
pairs.id: Di sebelah kanan, Anda bisa melihat …

steps.title: Menjelaskan grafik
steps.text: Baca keras-keras, pelan-pelan, dengan jeda singkat sebelum setiap angka.
steps.body: Slide-nya, dalam bentuk tabel (angka latihan): pengguna bulanan sebuah aplikasi makanan di Bandung · Januari 20.000 · April 35.000 · Juli 50.000 · Oktober 48.000. Perhatikan tiga langkahnya: apa yang ditunjukkan, ke mana harus melihat, dan pesannya.

examples.en: This graph shows the number of monthly users of our app in Bandung.
examples.id: Grafik ini menunjukkan jumlah pengguna bulanan aplikasi kita di Bandung.

examples.en: As you can see, the number of users rose steadily from January to July.
examples.id: Seperti yang bisa Anda lihat, jumlah pengguna naik terus dari Januari sampai Juli.

examples.en: In July, it peaked at fifty thousand, and then it fell slightly.
examples.id: Di bulan Juli, jumlahnya mencapai puncak di lima puluh ribu, lalu turun sedikit.

examples.en: What's interesting here is that the number more than doubled in just six months.
examples.id: Yang menarik di sini adalah jumlahnya naik lebih dari dua kali lipat hanya dalam enam bulan.

steps.title: Presentasikan slide-nya
steps.text: Sekarang kamu yang mempresentasikan slide.

question.prompt: Slide-mu (angka latihan): pesanan per bulan · Surabaya: Januari 2.000, Juni 4.000 · Bandung: Januari 3.000, Juni 3.000. Cara mana yang paling baik untuk membahasnya?
options: Okay, next. This is the chart. Surabaya, two thousand, four thousand. Bandung, three thousand, three thousand.
As you can see, orders in Surabaya rose until 4,000, while orders in Bandung fell sharply.
As you can see, orders in Surabaya doubled, from 2,000 to 4,000, while orders in Bandung remained stable.
question.explanation: Kalimat ini menunjuk slide-nya (*As you can see*), menyampaikan pesannya (*doubled*, *remained stable*) dan sesuai dengan angkanya. Yang pertama hanya membacakan angka. Yang kedua memakai *until* untuk level (katakan *rose to 4,000*), dan Bandung tidak turun: tetap di 3.000.

steps.title: Menjawab pertanyaan
steps.text: Bagian terakhir: pertanyaan di akhir presentasi. Ini rencana sederhananya.
steps.body: Empat langkah: **sambut** (*That's a great question.*), **cek** kalau kamu tidak yakin (*If I understand correctly, you're asking …?*), **jawab dengan singkat**, lalu **cek kembali** (*Does that answer your question?*). Tidak tahu? **Jangan pura-pura tahu** (bluffing): *I'm afraid I don't have that figure with me, but I'll follow up by email.* **I'm afraid** = sayangnya, cara sopan menyampaikan kabar kurang enak, bukan *takut*. Tindak lanjut yang jujur terdengar profesional; tebakan yang salah merusak kepercayaan orang.

pairs.en: If I understand correctly, you're asking …
pairs.id: Kalau saya tidak salah tangkap, Anda bertanya …

pairs.en: I'm afraid I don't have that figure with me.
pairs.id: Sayangnya saya tidak membawa angka itu.
Akan saya tindak lanjuti lewat email.

pairs.en: I'll check and get back to you.
pairs.id: Akan saya cek lalu saya kabari.

pairs.en: I'll come to that in a minute.

steps.title: Dengar dan jawab
steps.text: Tekan play dan dengarkan pertanyaan dari audiens.

question.prompt: Kamu sedang mempresentasikan penjualan tahun ini di kantormu di Jakarta. Kamu tidak membawa angka untuk setiap kota. Dengarkan pertanyaannya. Jawaban mana yang paling baik?
question.listen: Thank you for the presentation. Could you tell us the exact sales figure for Medan in December?
options: Sales in Medan were about two billion rupiah, I think. Maybe a bit more.
That's a good question. I'm afraid I don't have the Medan figure with me, but I'll check it and send it to you by email today.
Sorry, I'm afraid of this question. Next question, please.
question.explanation: Kamu tidak punya angkanya, jadi jujurlah: sambut pertanyaannya, katakan **I'm afraid** (sayangnya) kamu tidak membawanya, dan janjikan tindak lanjut. Jawaban pertama adalah tebakan, dan kalau salah, orang berhenti memercayai angka-angkamu. Yang ketiga, *I'm afraid of this question* artinya 'saya takut dengan pertanyaan ini', dan sama sekali tidak menjawab.

steps.title: Cek pertanyaannya
steps.text: Satu lagi: pertanyaan yang tidak sepenuhnya kamu pahami.

question.prompt: Di sebuah seminar di Yogyakarta, seorang mahasiswi mengajukan pertanyaan panjang tentang harga, pengiriman dan tahun depan. Kamu tidak yakin apa yang sebenarnya ingin dia ketahui. Apa jawaban pertama yang paling baik?
options: Yes. Next question, please.
If I understand correctly, you're asking whether delivery will cost more next year?
Sorry, I don't understand your English.
question.explanation: Cek dulu sebelum menjawab: **If I understand correctly, you're asking …?** menunjukkan kamu mendengarkan dan memberi dia kesempatan untuk membetulkan. *Next question* mengabaikannya, dan *I don't understand your English* menyalahkannya; kalau perlu, katakan *Sorry, I'm not sure I follow* (dari pelajaran rapat).

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini semuanya dalam satu halaman. Buka terus saat kamu menyiapkan presentasi berikutnya.
